notes: Finish the 10-minute teaser. If using scripted tool selection or recorded data, say so. A card should show source/freshness, and estimates must not masquerade as airline schedules. Show the factory verdict separately if the end-to-end bridge is unavailable.

title: What makes this an AI agent?
sub: It can use tools to help answer a question.
body:
You ask

“Will I make my 6 pm meeting?”

A language model interprets the request.

The application acts

It collects missing details, calls permitted tools and uses their results in its answer.
notes: 1 minute. A language model generates language; the surrounding application supplies instructions, conversation state and tools. Today tool selection is scripted for repeatability. Ask: can fluent wording tell us when a plane lands? No: we need a source.

title: A tool brings in information.
sub: A tool is a function the agent can ask the application to run.
body:
QuestionTool resultVisible answer
When does my flight land?Flight status and arrival timeFlight card
What happens after landing?Arrival time + your transfer allowanceArrival timeline
What will I need there?Weather and exchange-rate sourcesWeather and currency cards
notes: 1 minute. A function is a named piece of code with inputs and outputs. A tool result can fail or be out of date. The timeline is an estimate using assumptions, not a live road journey prediction.

title: Rasa Mantle runs the conversation.
sub: Mantle is the framework used to build our travel agent.
body:
It coordinates the work

Ask a language model to understand the request.
Keep track of the conversation.
Choose a skill and call its tools.
Apply instructions and constraints.

We supply the application

An OpenAI API key for the model.
Travel instructions and tools.
Connections to data sources.
The code that draws the four cards.
notes: 2 minutes. Define framework: reusable software that gives our application its structure. Define skill: a focused set of instructions and tools for a job, here preparing a travel briefing. Mantle does not provide this flight dashboard automatically. Mantle has no model of its own, so it asks a language model (OpenAI by default) to understand the request and choose a tool. Our exercises also have a scripted mode where teaching code chooses the tools; do not imply a live model made every decision there.

notes: 1 minute. Show these stages in the typed teaser. Conversation state means details remembered across turns. If the traveler says no to a suggested flight, the corrected demo lets them choose another. Ask: which stage should report a missing weather source? The tool result and visible answer.

title: The coding agent has a different job.
sub: The travel agent answers a traveler. The builder changes software.
body:
Travel agent

“Will I make my meeting?”

Doesn't need permission to edit code.

Builder

Proposes a change to product files.
Must not control the deciding tests.
notes: 1 minute. Ask the room which role needs file-writing permission. Today these are separate exercises. Asking the travel agent to change itself is not a completed workshop capability.

title: The OpenAI Agents API runs a builder session.
sub: An API is an interface one program uses to ask another service to do work.
body:
Our application sendsA task, agent configuration and execution environment.
The service runsA model session that can use configured tools.
Our application receivesProgress and results, then checks the proposed files.
Our application still ownsPermissions, independent checks, recovery and release decisions.
notes: 2 minutes. Session means one managed run of the agent’s work. The optional live builder uses this service; the default workshop builder is repeatable and needs no OpenAI key. Use gpt-6-astra for the documented optional live run; mention cost before starting.

title: Agents API and Agents SDK are different.
sub: This workshop uses the service through a Python client.
body:
Agents APIThe OpenAI service managing the session.
OpenAI Python clientCode our application uses to call that service.
Agents SDKA separate framework that this workshop does not teach.
MCPA protocol for exposing tools to agents. It is neither a builder nor a dashboard.
notes: 1 minute. Define protocol as an agreed format for requests and responses. MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. These names describe different responsibilities, not competing names for the same component. Runnable code is in chapter 5; do not begin with an incomplete API snippet.

title: What is a software factory?
sub: A repeatable process from a written request to a checked change.
body:
1 · Specify“Display three currency rows, with the reference date.”
2 · BuildA coding agent produces an attempt.
3 · CheckIndependent acceptance tests compare behavior with the request.
4 · DecideAccept or reject; integrate only an accepted attempt.
notes: 2 minutes. Candidate or attempt means the proposed files, not the final product. Acceptance test means an executable check of a requirement. The product is the travel application; the factory is the process for changing it. This is our workshop definition, not a claim that the label has a universal standard.

title: What makes a factory “dark”?
sub: Routine building and checking run without someone reviewing every line.
body:
People set the rules

What may change?
What must pass?
When should work stop for help?

Machines follow the rules

Build within that scope.
Run independent checks.
Keep evidence for the decision.
notes: 2 minutes. The term comes from factories able to operate without people on the production floor. Here it describes bounded automation, not the absence of human responsibility. A production system also needs release policy, monitoring and recovery. Today we practice one small local slice.

title: Try the rule before the code.
sub: Request: display exactly three currency rows.
body:
Attempt outputDecisionReason
Four rowsREJECTThe requested limit was not respected.
Three rows, reference date presentCheck all remaining requirementsOne visible success isn't the whole suite.
All required checks passACCEPTThis attempt meets the specified checks.
notes: 1 minute. Ask participants to predict the first decision before revealing it. This is a teaching example; the supplied chapter 5 task starts with limit 2, and its learner checkpoint asks you to build fresh with 1 or 3.

title: The builder can't grade its own homework.
sub: A separate checker decides, using tests the builder can’t change.
body:
The task and the product files

It may change only the allowed files.
It can run example tests.

proposed change

The acceptance tests

They decide ACCEPT or REJECT.
A fingerprint, a short code made from the files, shows nothing was swapped.

The builder may see example tests. It never sees or edits the acceptance tests that decide.
notes: 1 minute. A copied directory is not an operating-system sandbox, so protect execution as well as files. Explain both logical separation and actual execution isolation. Hashes detect mismatches but are not permissions. The existing Python code gate uses macOS sandbox-exec; the fallback checks JSON as data.

title: A completed session still needs a decision.
sub: A setup failure is different from a bad product.
body:
01

ACCEPT

The attempt passed the specified checks. Release checks still follow.

02

REJECT

A product requirement failed. Change the proposal and try again.

03

NOT_READY (could not run)

A dependency, account or verifier failed. No product verdict exists.
notes: 1 minute. Ask for examples of each result. A timed-out API request cannot be labeled REJECT solely because the provider failed. Passing a suite is bounded evidence, not proof of all future behavior.

title: Check your understanding with a neighbor.
sub: Explain the process without using the word “AI”.
body:
Who does what?

Who answers the traveler?
Who changes product files?
Who decides whether a change passes?

What if the builder says “done”?

What evidence would you ask for?
Which failure should stop the run?
Who handles an exception?
notes: 2 minutes, including answers. Travel agent answers; builder proposes files; independent verifier applies the tests. Builder completion is not acceptance. NOT_READY means the check could not run. People own exception policy. Allow someone to say what remains unclear before forming groups.

title: Release exactly the version that passed.
sub: If the code changes after the check, the check no longer counts.
body:
Version A

The change, its tests and their result

→

Is it still version A?

Same starting code? A quick start-up test passes?

→

The checked version

Live, with a way to roll back

A voice factory would also start the new agent and test it before anyone uses it.
notes: Optional table-side slide. An attempt accepted before integration may fail after integration. The supplied chapter 7 demonstrates local integration and stale-base refusal; it does not implement live deployment.

title: Voice has its own acceptance tests.
sub: Passing text tests leaves important behavior untested.
body:
01

A short reply

Does “yes” become the right confirmed action?

02

An interruption

Does playback stop while the user changes the request?

03

A failed source

Does speech explain the problem while the board keeps useful data?
notes: Explanation only today: Voice was tested with Deepgram audio files today and failed on the second turn, so type your requests. The microphone path is untested. Optional later: check ASR, TTS, timing, interruption and state retention. The version update uses deepgram_flux for Flux ASR and deepgram for Aura-2 TTS. If voice falls back to text, mark voice incomplete.

title: The next step is the complete build-to-voice journey.
sub: Ask for a new agent by voice, and get a checked one you can try.
body:
A travel agent and a separate builder

Real data sources, cards, a factory that checks a change, and a way to bring an accepted change into the product.

A voice factory that releases what it builds

Ask by voice, follow the build, cancel it if needed, start exactly the checked version, and test it by voice.
notes: Close honestly. Reference BUILD-CONTRACT.md for the remaining implementation and scenarios. A scaffold-based factory is valid, but we must say what the scaffold supplied and what the builder changed.
